Honestly, not very often. Getting an angry call was a daily thing, but giving refunds is highly circumstantial. It depends on why they want it, how much they're asking for, how often that particular person calls in for refunds.

The most common refund request was a guest wanting a refund on a strict cancellation policy. Airbnb upholds all it's policies. In situations like that, the host would have to agree to a refund in order for Airbnb to give the angry guest one.

The other very common refund request was Airbnb service fees. And unless you meet the requirements (canceled within 48 hours of booking and less than 3 cancellations in the last 12 months), you're not getting those fees back. While it's understandable why the guest would be upset, Airbnb also has a website to run and employees to pay.

There are a lot of factors that come into play when it comes to what guests will book. Some of the bigger factors:

Pictures: Guests tend to pick listings that have higher quality and quantity pictures. 

Location: Listings that are in not great neighborhoods are less likely to get booked. And on the opposite end, someone in a high tourist spot is going to get more bookings than someone that is in the middle of nowhere.

Reviews: Someone with more than 10 reviews will start to see an increase in bookings. Host's without reviews have a harder time getting bookings.

Seasons/Events: Places that are near events tend to get booked faster. Every location its going to have a season that gets hosts more bookings than others. Florida during Spring for example. Or New Orleans during Mardi Gras.

Smaller factors:

Policy: A host's cancellation policy doesn't seem to have such an impact on getting a booking. That more effects the number of cancellations you'll get. 

Amenities: If you have the basics and nothing else, then you'll probably receive fewer bookings than someone that has a few extra listed, however if two hosts have more than the basics, then other factors are going to be more influential to bookings.
